Edited by Florence Vere-Laurie and printed in 1921, this volume gathers the letters of Lieutenant-Colonel George Brenton Laurie, commanding the 1st Battalion, Royal Irish Rifles. Written from France between November 4, 1914, and March 11, 1915, they form a diary of the first winter of the World War.

Laurie wrote often under fire, telling his wife of heavy losses, bitter cold, and the daily work of his regiment. Parcels from home, mince pies, and bales of clothing break the gloom, and his cheerful tone lifts many a page. He fell the next day, March 12, 1915, at Neuve Chapelle. The letters stand as a plain, moving record of a battalion commander at war.
